samples.marker_line: COM installer: hidden task, updater disguise and Defender exclusion
execution_trace: Copies the argument-supplied executable into a newly generated 12-character alphanumeric directory under C:\ProgramData as MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe.

Registers RuntimeBroker with Task Scheduler COM, using a logon trigger repeating every 15 minutes for P3650D. The action points at the copied executable. Hidden=true and ExecutionTimeLimit=PT0S conceal the task and remove its runtime limit.

Uses InteractiveToken and LeastPrivilege; it does not request elevation. Only when the current token is already Administrator does it start hidden PowerShell to add a Defender exclusion for that directory.
The sole HTTP string is the task XML namespace, not a network request. No payload download or immediate launch of the copied executable is present.
samples.decision_evidence: Trusted-product disguise of an arbitrary supplied image, hidden recurring persistence, and conditional protection bypass together outweigh an ordinary updater-install explanation.
missing_context: Source executable and its contents, operator authorization, installation history and runtime success are unavailable.
samples.coverage: Two accurate suspicious traits cover persistence and Defender exclusion. Neither generic pattern alone justifies a hostile rule; no fabricated payload capability was added.

samples.marker_line: P7 reconstruction: remote exec and file theft; corrected loader claim
execution_trace: The header explicitly describes a reconstruction, not recovered spyware. No browser exploit, native keychain extraction, or supply-chain substitution is implemented.

Creates a 15-second poll timer, then calls uploadSecrets. readKeychain reads and JSON-parses /private/var/tmp/keychain_c2_dump.json, and the parsed value becomes the keychain field in an HTTPS POST to agdx53.cc/war.

poll POSTs the PID to /beacon, parses the response, and switches on task.command. exec evaluates task.code in local scope and POSTs its result to /result. download reads task.path and sends the file bytes to /result.

sleep replaces the timer using the server-provided seconds; exit clears the timer rather than exiting the process. Initial collection requires the dump file to exist; errors are not caught and runtime success was not established.

Cleave flow facts trace fetch -> reply.json -> task.code -> eval, eval -> result -> JSON.stringify -> fetch.body, and reply.json -> task.path -> readFileSync -> fetch.body. No specimen was run against its endpoint.
samples.decision_evidence: Despite the research/reconstruction label, active code sends a secret dump to an external endpoint and offers arbitrary remote execution and file reads without a local authorization gate. These concrete operations tip the judgment.
missing_context: Whether the dump contains real secrets, endpoint availability, execution history and the user's authorization are unknown.
No claim that this is a recovered production P7 implant or that the file was installed as a dependency.
samples.coverage: Two hostile traits cover remote code tasking/result reporting and HTTP-selected file upload with remote execution. Keychain-named-helper upload remains suspicious because its matcher cannot establish native keychain access.

samples.marker_line: Research probe: startup env/proc/cloud spying; corrected hook claim
execution_trace: Original wheel SHA-256 and every hashed RECORD member verified. METADATA names research-probe-6150c1c915 0.1.0 with the generic summary research project. Root-Is-Purelib=true; a root .pth imports research_probe_6150c1c915._boot.

Importing _boot executes bootstrap() at module scope. _snapshot collects uid/gid, hostname, working directory, executable, argv, sys.path, boot/uptime data, every environment value truncated to 200 characters, and up to 200 processes with command lines.

Bounded daemon threads probe TCP reachability to six targets, resolve three hostnames, GET the PyPI index, request recursive GCP metadata and default service-account email using Metadata-Flavor: Google. The join budget is 2.5 seconds. No explicit service-account token endpoint is requested.

bootstrap serializes the snapshot and writes run-<time>-<pid>.json both under the installed package's _runs directory and /tmp/<package>. Errors are swallowed. __init__.py exposes runs() to retrieve the local snapshots.

There is no upload of the collected report, remote command execution, or explicit cloud access-token theft in these bytes. Startup surveying is concrete; a remote exfiltration claim would be unsupported.

A controlled execution of parsed function definitions with fake OS, sockets, DNS, HTTP and file I/O confirmed sentinel environment/process arguments in two writes, six TCP attempts, three DNS lookups and three GET requests. No real sample I/O was allowed.
samples.decision_evidence: An automatically installed interpreter-startup hook records potentially sensitive environment/process data and cloud metadata without an explicit invocation. Its generic research label does not explain collecting every process startup. The narrow external advisory corroborates shared-infrastructure reconnaissance with local storage.
missing_context: Operator access to the snapshots, user consent, install history and successful metadata responses are unknown. Local storage is not proof of remote exfiltration.

forager fetch --all-wheels was attempted for the exact PURL. PyPI metadata returned 404; the browser fallback failed because Chromium ICU data was unavailable. The supplied original wheel was examined; no replacement artifact was synthesized.
samples.coverage: Three suspicious traits cover module-call/survey code, startup-hook/cloud request co-occurrence, and startup-hook/host-cloud snapshot co-occurrence. Shared matchers cannot bind the import to the collector, so no hostile startup rule is claimed; the direct .pth-to-_boot-to-bootstrap trace establishes this specimen's spying behavior.

source.supports: Startup reconnaissance of shared infrastructure; data stored locally. Campaign-level cloud-token claims are not attributed to the examined wheel.

shared_rule_audit: All exact and ancestor consumers inspected for the relocated and renamed rules. Supply-chain module-init has no ancestor/exact consumer of the removed composite. Existing remote-evaluation and module-call observations retain their matchers.

Neutral updater-name atoms and their explicit OR composite moved with identical patterns/scope/severity to fs/path/basename; the writable-location and persistent-tunnel consumers now reference the new canonical ID. Attack/masquerade mappings removed from the neutral names.

The PowerShell URL literal moved unchanged to http/url/scheme. Its endpoint and credential-export consumers and the established inert-reference control were updated. The remaining http/message parent consumer is Ruby-only and cannot gain or lose PowerShell evidence; the destination URL-scheme consumer is shell/Python-only.

New basename membership affects broad filesystem selectors; their other required evidence is absent in these specimens/controls. Existing PE-only consumers cannot gain script evidence. The CrystalX C2 exclusion is PE-only and cannot gain the new JS-only dispatch rules.

Discovery ancestor consumers retain the same match sets; the imported-snapshot rename and startup co-occurrence correction do not add or remove archive findings. ATT&CK mappings no longer imply shell initialization or access-token theft.

Before correction the separate uncalled CDN plugin-loader control matched a hostile supply-chain claim. The unrelated-import control wheel, carrying the real survey code but importing harmless.py, matched a hostile startup-to-survey claim. Both observations are retained as suspicious accurately described co-occurrences.

Four out-of-batch remote-evaluation fixtures retain every finding and severity, including the hostile ghappier module-response loader. Existing file-task upload and native-store positive/negative controls pass.
material_losses: Unsupported hostile supply-chain/automatic-load claim replaced by suspicious HTTP-eval/module-call context; no remote-evaluation capability lost. Added distinct hostile code-task/result-upload coverage.
Unsupported hostile .pth-to-survey relationship replaced by suspicious co-occurrence; all wheel/member observations preserved. No benign import exception was introduced.
classifier_limitations: The PowerShell classifier becomes BENIGN despite retaining exactly two suspicious and 32 notable observations at unchanged severity. This is a classifier miss after accurate taxonomy relocation, not a reason to restore misplaced traits.
The wheel parent remains HOSTILE but _boot.py independently remains ML BENIGN despite the reviewed suspicious survey finding; archive context and manual execution-path analysis establish its role.
Atomscan warns that its feature/model spec is v18 while the extractor expects v19. Probabilities are recorded as observations, not verdict evidence.
